patterns_extracted.name: ZOD_DISCRIMINATED_UNION_MESSAGES
patterns_extracted.evidence: WebSocket protocol uses z.discriminatedUnion('action', [wsClientSubscribeSchema, wsClientUnsubscribeSchema, wsClientPingSchema]) for type-safe client->server messages. Server responses use z.discriminatedUnion('type', [...]) with welcome/subscribed/error/pong/event types.
patterns_extracted.impact: Eliminates runtime type errors in message routing, enables exhaustive type checking at compile time

patterns_extracted.name: PER_CLIENT_SUBSCRIPTION_STATE
patterns_extracted.evidence: EventBroadcaster tracks subscriptions per client via Map<clientId, Set<EventType>>. subscribe() and unsubscribe() operations are atomic. broadcast() filters clients by subscription before sending.
patterns_extracted.impact: Clients only receive events they care about, reducing network load. Subscription state persists across message handling.

antipatterns_found.name: NON_FUNCTIONAL_OWNERSHIP_FILTERING
antipatterns_found.evidence: Iterations 1-2 included userId filtering logic in WebSocket message validation, checking 'userId in payload'. However, no events actually included userId (terminal:output has {sessionId, data}, feature:* events are just action objects). Dead code was removed in iteration 3.
antipatterns_found.root_cause: Premature optimization: assumed multi-user filtering model without business requirement or supporting data
antipatterns_found.resolution: Simplified to all-authenticated-users model appropriate for single-user desktop app

key_insights.insight: Type-safe message protocols reduce iteration cycles
key_insights.details: Discriminated unions caught message shape mismatches early. Only 3 iterations (2 on requirements, 1 on implementation details).

key_insights.insight: Subscription model validated during Phase 4 review
key_insights.details: Code review findings (4 non-blocking) included verifying per-client filtering works correctly. No security issues detected.

key_insights.insight: Unit test coverage at 100% for WebSocket handlers
key_insights.details: 24 tests cover open, message routing (subscribe/unsubscribe/ping), error handling, client removal. Terminal WebSocket integration handled separately in F092.
useWebSocket hook sends full subscription list on reconnect. Server responds with 'subscribed' confirmation. Prevents silent subscription loss.

architecture_notes.server_layer: Hono WebSocket handler with auth enforcement (401 reject on upgrade if not authenticated)
architecture_notes.client_lib: WebSocketClient singleton in apps/web/src/lib/websocket.ts with auto-reconnection and heartbeat (ping/pong)
architecture_notes.react_hooks: useWebSocket for connection state, useEventSubscription for typed event listeners

recommendations_for_downstream.recommendation: Reuse WsClientMessage and WsServerMessage schemas from F034. Define new event types in event.ts (e.g., 'agent:chunk', 'agent:tool-call'). Client can subscribe to these via existing useEventSubscription hook.

Current WebSocket handler separates 'events' and 'terminal' channels. Terminal channel uses sessionId-based client grouping. Can extend with 'terminal:input' client message type for bidirectional input.
Subscribe to all event types via useEventSubscription. Filter/store in local state or Zustand. EventBroadcaster does not persist history (by design for memory efficiency).
